intake.bucket:
LM-299 (also designated MK-2010 by Merck)

Bispecific antibody targeting PD-1 and VEGF simultaneously.

Originated by LaNova Medicines / Genomeditech, a subsidiary of Sino Biopharm.
Merck acquired exclusive global rights (ex-China).
Deal: $588M upfront, up to $2.7B in milestones, $300M technology transfer.

Mechanism: Dual blockade — blocks PD-1 immune checkpoint signaling AND VEGF-mediated angiogenesis in a single molecule. Combines what Keytruda does (PD-1) with what Avastin/bevacizumab does (VEGF).

Architecture: sdAb-based (single-domain antibody / nanobody) bispecific format. Different from ivonescimab's conventional antibody format.

Target Indications: Advanced solid tumors, non-small cell lung cancer, immuno-oncology broadly.

Development Stage: Phase 1 clinical trial. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06650566. Enrolling in China for advanced malignant tumors.

Jurisdictions: US, China, EU, Japan

Competitors:
- Ivonescimab (Akeso/Summit) — PD-1/VEGF bispecific, Phase 3, potential FDA approval Nov 2026
- BNT327 (BioNTech) — another PD-1/VEGF bispecific in development
- Keytruda (pembrolizumab) — Merck's own PD-1 mono, patent cliff 2028

Strategic context: LM-299 is Merck's next-generation play for the post-Keytruda era. If it works, it's a biologically distinct molecule — not pembrolizumab, not biosimilar-able — that could absorb Keytruda's indications with a superior dual-blockade efficacy argument. New composition-of-matter patents, new data exclusivity, new IRA clock.

Problem: LM-299 is 4-5 years behind class leader ivonescimab. The market may be defined before LM-299 arrives.

Not yet in PubChem or DrugBank (too early stage). Not in FDA databases. Only in ClinicalTrials.gov and AdisInsight.

INVENTOR CLAIMS — WO2024125417A1 (Lanova Medicines Ltd)
Filed: 2023-12-08 | Priority: 2022-12-12 | Published: 2024-06-20

INDEPENDENT CLAIM 1 (Composition):
A bispecific antibody comprising an anti-VEGF portion and an anti-PD-1 portion, wherein:

(a) the anti-VEGF portion comprises an anti-VEGF antibody or antigen binding fragment having binding specificity to a human VEGF protein, which comprises:
  - a heavy chain variable region (VH) comprising:
    - CDRH1 comprising the amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 9
    - CDRH2 comprising the amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 10
    - CDRH3 comprising the amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 11
  - a light chain variable region (VL) comprising:
    - CDRL1 comprising the amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 12
    - CDRL2 comprising the amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 13
    - CDRL3 comprising the amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 14

(b) the anti-PD-1 portion comprises an anti-PD-1 single domain antibody (VHH/nanobody) having binding specificity to a human PD-1 protein, which comprises:
  - CDR1 comprising the amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 5
  - CDR2 comprising the amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 6
  - CDR3 comprising the amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 7 (VH18 variant) or SEQ ID NO: 8 (VH8M1 variant)

DEPENDENT CLAIM ELEMENTS (from specification):
- The VH of the anti-VEGF portion comprises the amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 3
- The VL of the anti-VEGF portion comprises the amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 4
- The anti-VEGF portion is a full size Fab antibody with IgG Fc fragment
- The IgG Fc fragment comprises LALA mutations (L234A, L235A, EU numbering)
- The anti-PD-1 single domain antibody comprises the amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 1 (VH18) or SEQ ID NO: 2 (VH8M1)
- The anti-PD-1 nanobody is fused to the C-terminal side of the anti-VEGF antibody via a (G4S)4 linker (SEQ ID NO: 15)
- The bispecific antibody comprises 2 anti-PD-1 VHH per molecule (B12D1-9/B12D1-10 variants) or 4 anti-PD-1 VHH per molecule (B12D1-6 variant)

INDEPENDENT CLAIM 2 (Composition/Formulation):
A pharmaceutical composition comprising the bispecific antibody and a pharmaceutically acceptable carrier.

INDEPENDENT CLAIM 3 (Method of Treatment):
A method of treating cancer in a patient in need thereof, comprising administering to the patient the bispecific antibody, wherein the cancer is selected from: bladder cancer, breast cancer, colorectal cancer, endometrial cancer, esophageal cancer, head and neck cancer, kidney cancer, leukemia, liver cancer, lung cancer, lymphoma, melanoma, pancreatic cancer, prostate cancer, and thyroid cancer.

KEY STRUCTURAL ELEMENTS FOR FTO COMPARISON:
1. Anti-VEGF portion = Bevacizumab-derived CDRs (SEQ ID NOs 9-14)
2. Anti-PD-1 portion = single domain antibody (VHH/nanobody), NOT conventional antibody
3. Architecture = nanobody fused to C-terminus of full-size IgG1 antibody
4. Linker = (G4S)4 (SEQ ID NO: 15)
5. Fc = IgG1 with LALA mutations (silenced effector function)
6. Variants: 2-VHH (B12D1-9, B12D1-10) or 4-VHH (B12D1-6)

• **Claim 3 (Method):** Cancer treatment method covering 16 tumor types — [RISK LEVEL: MODERATE] for method-only overlap analysis

• **Architecture differentiator:** Nanobody fused to C-terminus of full-size IgG1 via (G4S)4 linker (SEQ ID NO: 15); LALA Fc mutations (L234A, L235A) — distinguishes from ivonescimab conventional antibody format

• **Design-around pathway:** Alternative linker chemistry, non-bevacizumab VEGF binding domains, or PD-1 binding domains outside disclosed CDR sequences require claim-chart verification by counsel

sections.title: Competitive Landscape & Pipeline
sections.content:
**Ivonescimab Defines the Class Leader Timeline**

• **Ivonescimab (Akeso/Summit):** PD-1/VEGF bispecific, Phase 3, PDUFA goal November 2026 — sets commercial and patent precedent for dual-target IO

• **BNT327 (BioNTech):** PD-1/VEGF bispecific in development — adjacency monitoring required

• **Keytruda (pembrolizumab):** Merck's own PD-1 monoclonal; patent cliff 2028 — LM-299 strategic context is post-Keytruda indication absorption with superior dual-blockade argument

**Clinical anchor:** NCT06650566 — Phase 1, advanced malignant tumors, enrolling in China. Not yet in FDA Orange Book.

sections.title: Strategic Signals & Counsel Next Steps
sections.content:
**Converging Signals Suggest Urgency on Class-Definition Timing**

1. LM-299 is 4–5 years behind ivonescimab — market definition risk before LM-299 approval
2. Composition-of-matter claims are sequence-specific — biosimilar pathway unlikely; new IRA/exclusivity clock if approved
3. VEGF portion derives from bevacizumab CDR sequences — cross-reference Avastin/bevacizumab estate during FTO prep

**Recommended counsel actions:**

• Pull full claim text for US20250019442A1 and EP4634236A1 directly from USPTO/EPO registers
• Element-by-element chart against inventor claims in intake (WO2024125417A1)
• Monitor ivonescimab FDA action (November 2026 PDUFA goal date — not an approval)
